translation:
|| Here begins the holy Kadavu ||4||

1. Hari, Hari — Kanhan (Krishna) of dark hue, let us sing of him: a broad tilak of musk upon his brow. The child is beautiful, exceedingly lovely. ||1||
2. Hariji's golden crown is charming; rubies beyond counting are set in it; diamonds flash there like the sun. ||2||
3. In Hariji's ears are earrings, at his throat a neck-band; upon his breast a garland of pearls; the garland with the Kaustubh gem blazes. ||3||
4. A pearl sways at Hariji's nose; jewelled bangles are on his hands; gem-studded armlets upon his arms. ||4||
5. Hariji wears a yellow silken robe; sandal paste is smeared on his breast; garlands and flower-tufts, blossoms in plenty. ||5||

|| Aad ||1||

1. Hari outwitted King Ambarish; he came down in incarnation as the occasion required — the Lord, in all ten avatars. ||1||
2. Hari stood at the door of Bali; though Bali looked, he did not grasp him — he who is beyond, the Lord of yogis. ||2||
3. Hari filled Sudama with riches — that supremely resourceful one; Sudama recognized in him the treasure-house of liberation. ||3||
4. Hari — perishable riches he did not embrace; he made everything steadfast, and took the witness of the Smriti (the remembered scripture). ||4||

|| Aad ||2||

1. Hari, Hari — say "Krishna, Krishna": Rukmini, night and day, is dyed in the virtues of Gopal. ||1||
2. Hari, Hari — he fulfilled the heart's longing of her, and crushed King Shishupal. ||2||
3. Hari, Hari — sixteen thousand maidens lay in prison; Narakasur had seized their very lives. ||3||
4. Hariji slew the demon and set the maidens free — the wielder of the discus (Chakrapani), who loves his devotees. ||4||

|| Aad ||3||

1. Pure and supreme knowledge; the Lord, the treasury of qualities and arts; a purifying place of pilgrimage — holy is the kirtan (hymn) of Hari. ||1||
2. The radiance of ten million suns; the Lord upholds the earth and the sky; victory, victory to Vishvambhar, the sustainer of all — Hari, who is terror to the demons. ||2||
3. Hari, the Supreme Self, Ram, whose Name is spotless for ever; the deliverer of the three worlds — Hari, who wards off hell. ||3||
4. The Great Death of death itself; the Lord Gopal who burns away sin; the beloved of Tulsi — Hari, hard to attain even for gods and men. ||4||

|| Aad ||4||

1. O Lord, you are the almighty father: avert this calamity. The little soul has been ruined by vain imagining — remove that first of all. ||1||
2. The blame lies upon the head of karma, but the matter is in your hands; unceasing remembrance of you breaks apart the whole mass of karma. ||2||
3. Driven by karma the soul has wandered and fled, into ever-new wombs without number — happy or wretched, highest or middling, all are the Lord's own servants. ||3||
4. Truly it heaps up new karma while it endures the old — thus there is no crossing beyond karma; but if you show your grace now, then this very moment there is release. ||4||
5. Thakor, you alone are father, you are brother, treasury of compassion; I am an offender destitute of your bhakti (devotion) — forgive me, Lord Govind, Kanhan. ||5||
6. Those whom you have saved before — great were their offences, yet all of them now sport in supreme bliss, because you, the almighty king, were pleased with them. ||6||
7. Now there is no fear of prakriti (material nature); I have served Kanhan of Gokul; my mind is absorbed in the contemplation of pure consciousness; the Name of Hari has burnt my karma away. ||7||
8. You are the master of my soul and my mind — I am not its master, not for a moment; take back your own possession into your keeping, for with me it is spoiled beyond measure. ||8||

|| Aad ||5||

1. Brahma spoke to Dharmaraj: do not open a quarrel with the great, do not utter unrighteousness — the Vaishnavas are Hari's own, and worthy of worship. ||1||
2. He on whose mouth is the nectar of Hari's Name, tulsi at his throat and gopichandan on his forehead — gods and men bow to him; Brahma declares him the pilgrimage-place of pilgrimage-places. ||2||
3. Even those who perform the worship of Shankar and the rest — that very instant they leave off from there, and come and fix their attention where the Vaishnava folk are: so Brahma declares. ||3||
4. Serve such an almighty one, devoted to his bhaktas and doing good to others; he alone is the stainless God (Niranjan); serve him, for he destroys the anguish of the womb. ||4||

|| Aad ||6||

1. O Hari, my Lord, O Hari, my Lord — Father, take care of me; this soul is in the power of birth and death. ||1||
2. Forgetting, forgetting — the Name of Hari, the Parbrahm; with an unheeding mind I have gone blind. ||2||
3. O Hari, my Lord, O my Lord — you are compassionate to the lowly; do not so forget this poor wretch. ||3||
4. Many, so many have I done — deeds done for my own sake; and hell and Yama are fearsome. ||4||
5. Exceedingly hard, exceedingly hard — great torments before this; in earlier births I have endured them. ||5||
6. In dread of that, in dread of that, O Lord, this soul has come to take refuge in you. ||6||
7. Now keep me, now keep me, Lord, within your own self; honour the word you yourself have given. ||7||

|| Aad ||7||

1. Hari, Parbrahm — Hari, Parbrahm — Lord, you are the Supreme Brahman; by good fortune I have obtained your japa (repetition of the Name). ||1||
2. Hari, the One alone — Hari, the One alone — Lord, fulfil my longing; may bhakti spring up in all that moves and all that moves not. ||2||
3. Set it up thus, set it up thus, Lord — an age of Vaikunth; in house after house let there be no other talk. ||3||
4. He has taken birth, he has taken birth — Kanhan of Gokul, Shri Padmanabh, Purushottam. ||4||
5. Whoever sings, whoever listens to this song bound upon Parbrahm — for him the bonds of worldly existence are loosed. ||5||

|| Aad ||8||

|| Thus the Kadavu is complete ||4||10

The second resting-place (vishram) of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.
